Brazil +55

Communication of 26.XI.2014

The Agência Nacional de Telecomunicações (ANATEL) , Brasilia, announces that the Numbering Plan of mobile services in Brazil will be modified due to the increasing demand for new numbers.

The current format of mobile numbers is N 8 N 7 N 6 N 5 N 4 N 3 N 2 N 1 and the first digit which identifies this service is 9, 8, 7 or 6. However, in accordance with Resolution No. 553, issued by the Agência Nacional de Telecomunicações (ANATEL) on 14 December 2010, there will be the inclusion of a ninth digit in mobile number length and all subscriber numbers will initiate with the digit “9”.

Therefore, mobile numbers will have the following format: +55 XX 9 XXXX XXXX (country code, area code and subscriber number).

This change was already implemented in the Area Codes 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18 and 19 (State of São Paulo), in the Area Codes 21, 22, 24, 27 and 28 (States of Rio de Janeiro and Espírito Santo) and in the Area Codes 91, 92, 93, 94, 95, 96, 97, 98 and 99 (States of Amapá, Amazonas, Maranhão, Pará and Roraima).

Now, in this year of 2015, the changing will occur in the Area Codes 81, 82, 83, 84, 85, 86, 87, 88, and 89 (States of Alagoas, Ceará, Paraiba, Pernambuco, Piauí, Rio Grande do Norte), on May 31 st ,   and in the Area Codes 31, 32, 33, 34, 35, 37 and 38 (State of Minas Gerais) and 71, 73, 74, 75, 77 and 79 (States of Bahia and Sergipe), on October 11 th .

ANATEL will define in the future the date in which this change will take place in the other Area Codes of Brazil.

In addition, ANATEL would like to highlight that this format change will not be applied to mobile radio service numbers nor to fixed switched telephone numbers. Consequently, subscriber numbers for these services will remain eight-digit long.

Cameroon +237

Communication of 6.X.2014

The Agence de Régulation des Télécommunications (ART), Yaoundé, announces that the National Numbering Plan (NNP) of Cameroon will migrate from eight (8) to nine (9) digits on Friday, 21 November 2014 at 22.59 UTC.

The new Cameroonian National Numbering Plan is a closed nine-digit plan with the following format:

CC N(S)N

where:

CC (country code) = +237

N(S)N (national (significant) number) consists of nine digits in the format SABPQMCDU

I) International incoming calls

International dialling format: (+237)(N(S)N). In the format +237 SABPQMCDU the digit “ S ” of the national (significant) number N(S)N represents the service.

II) National Numbering Plan

The National Numbering Plan is a closed nine-digit plan in the format SABPQMCDU organized according to services. A distinction is made between two main types of number: mobile telephone numbers and fixed telephone numbers.

a.          Mobile telephone numbers

The number blocks for which the value of area code " S " is equal to " 6 " are reserved for mobile telephone services.

Examples:

+ 237 6X XX XX XX becomes + 237 6 6X XX XX XX for a mobile number of the NEXTTEL (ex VIETTEL) network;

+ 237 7X XX XX XX becomes + 237 6 7X XX XX XX for a mobile number of the MTN Cameroon network;

+ 237 9X XX XX XX becomes + 237 6 9X XX XX XX for a mobile number of the Orange Cameroun network.

b.          Fixed telephone numbers

The number blocks for which the value of area code "S" is equal to “2” are reserved for fixed telephone networks and services with restricted mobility. A distinction is made between geographic numbers with prefixes 2 22 XX XX XX and 2 33 XX XX XX and CDMA telephone numbers with prefixes 2 42 XX XX XX or 2 43 XX  XX XX.

Communication of 11.VIII.2014

The Autorité de Régulation des Télécommunications & des Postes (ARTP ), Dakar, announces the following update of the National Numbering Plan (NNP) of Senegal. The Numbering Plan of Senegal is a closed plan with nine (9) digits with the following format:

CC N(S)N

Where:

CC (Country Code ) = +221 N(S)N (National (Significant) Number) will consist of nine (9) digits: SABPQMCDU

International numbering format: CC (221) + N(S)N (nine digits)

III.         Outgoing international calls

In order to make an international call from Senegal, dial the international prefix “00” and then the number in the following format:

              00 CC NDC SN, where:

CC

=

Country Code

NDC

=

National Destination Code

SN

=

Subscriber Number

 

IV.         Non-geographical numbers (convergent services: IP telephony, etc.).

These numbers take the form SABPQMCDU, in which S = 9.

V.                   National calls

In order to call a subscriber to the national fixed or mobile telecommunication networks (local or national call), a number of format SABPQMCDU is used.

VI.         Calls to emergency services

The numbers used to contact one of the emergency services (two or three digits) from within the country take the following format:

1X - where        X = 8 fire service and X = 7 police

These services cannot be called from outside the country.

Communication of 7.VII.2014

The Autorité de Régulation des Communications électroniques et des Postes (ARCEP ), Libreville, announces that, at the request of the telephony operators, the final phase of the changeover to the national eight-digit telephone numbering plan, which will involve removing the 0 after the country code 241 for international calls to Gabon and was originally to have taken place on Tuesday, 1 July 2014 , has been postponed to a later date.

Iran (Islamic Republic of) +98

Communication of 7.VII.2014

The Communications Regulatory Authority (CRA) , Tehran, announces the following changes to the National Numbering Plan of Iran.

Presentation of the Iran E.164 numbering plan

1. General Information

The E.164 numbering Plan of Iran:

  • Country Code: +98

  • International Prefix: “00”

  • National Prefix: ”0”

For national calls, it must be dialled before all telephone numbers except short numbers. It must not be dialled from abroad.

  • National destination Code: 2-3 digits.

2. Detail of Numbering Scheme

  • NDC: National Destination Code

  • NSN: National Significant Number (NDC + SN)

The minimum number length (excluding the country code) is: 7 digits

The maximum number length (excluding the country code) is: 10 digits

Netherlands +31

Communication of 6.VI.2014

The Authority for Consumers and Markets (ACM), The Hague , announces the updated ITU-T E.164 National Numbering Plan for Netherlands.

1. Unless explicitly determined otherwise in the destination associated with a number, a number included in this numbering plan shall not be used to provide paid services other than electronic communications services if the payment of those services is included in the invoice prepared by the provider of the electronic communications service.

2. The length of a geographic number is ten digits and the length of a non-geographic number can vary.

3. A geographic number in which the subscriber number begins with the digits 0,1 or 9 is not available for assignment or reservation .

4. A number from the 014 range is available without assignment or reservation, contrary to that stated at the top of the table 1.

5. A geographic or non-geographic number may not consist of another, shorter or longer, geographic or non-geographic number followed by one or more digits.

6. Since June 1st the +31 970 XXXX XXXX is obligatory for operators for applications that are mobile data-only and do not have a mobile telephony function for voice calling.

7. The former Numbering Plan for Telephone and ISDN Services (Government Gazette 1996, 144) shall be revoked.

Table 3 – Conditions on the right to use the numbers in the 116 numbering range

Number

Qualification of the service and conditions for entitlement for use

116…

a) The service provides the citizen with information or assistance or a reporting tool, or a combination thereof. b) The service is accessible for all citizens without any prior registration requirements. c) The service is not limited in time. d) To be able to make use of the service, no advance payment or commitment to payment is required. e) During a call there shall be no advertisements, amusement, marketing or sales. Similarly, the call shall not be used for the purposes of selling commercial services in the future.

116000

a) The service receives notifications by telephone of missing children and passes them on to the police. b) The service gives advice/assistance and supports the parents/guardians of the missing child. c) The service supports investigations. d) The service is continually available (24 hours per day, 7 days a week, across the whole country)

116006

a) The service enables victims of crime to get emotional support in such circumstances, to be informed about their rights and about ways to claim their rights, and to be referred to the relevant organisations.

b) In particular, it provides information about local police and criminal justice proceedings, and the possibilities of compensation and insurance matters.

c) It also provides support in finding other sources of help relevant to the victims of crime.

d) Where the service is not continuously available (i.e. 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, nation-wide), the service provider must ensure that information about availability is made publicly available in an easily accessible form, and that, during periods of unavailability, callers to the service are advised when the service will next become available.

116111

a) The service helps children in need of care and protection and refers them to the appropriate services and facilities. b) The service offers children the opportunity to express their concerns, and to talk about matters which directly concern them, and to contact someone when an emergency occurs c) If the service is not continuously available (24 hours per day, 7 days per week, across the whole country), the service provider must ensure that the information about accessibility is available in a manner that is easily accessible to the public, and that during periods when the service is not available, callers are informed of when the service will again be accessible.

116117

a) The service directs callers to the medical assistance appropriate to their needs, which are urgent but non-life-threatening, especially, but not exclusively, outside normal office hours, over the weekend and on public holidays.

b) It connects the caller to a skilled and supported call-handler, or connects the caller directly to a qualified medical practitioner or clinician.

c) Where the service is not continuously available (i.e. 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, nation-wide), the service provider must ensure that information about availability is made publicly available in an easily accessible form, and that, during periods of unavailability, callers to the service are advised when the service will next become available.

116123

a) This service enables the caller to make direct human contact whereby they are listened to objectively. b) The service offers emotional support to callers who are lonely, undergoing a psychological crisis or considering suicide. c) If the service is not continuously available (24 hours per day, 7 days per week, across the whole country), the service provider must ensure that the information about accessibility is available in a manner that is easily accessible to the public, and that during periods when the service is not available, callers are informed of when the service will again be accessible.

The Autorité de Régulation des Télécommunications & des Postes (ARTP ), Dakar, announces the following update of the National Numbering Plan (NNP) of Senegal. The Numbering Plan of Senegal is a closed plan with nine (9) digits with the following format:

              CC N(S)N

Where:

              CC (Country Code ) = +221               N(S)N (National (Significant) Number) will consist of nine digits: SABPQMCDU

I.  Incoming international calls

1.          International numbering format: CC (221) + N(S)N (nine digits)

Mobile telephony numbers

Blocks of numbers for which “S” is “7” are reserved for the mobile telephony networks.

–            The list of numbers SABPQMCDU currently allocated to the universal operator service EXPRESSO Sénégal for its mobile phone network is as follows:

III. Outgoing international calls

In order to make an international call from Senegal, dial the international prefix “00” and then the number in the following format:

00 CC NDC SN,

where: 

CC

=

Country Code

NDC

=

National Destination Code

SN

=

Subscriber Number

 

IV.  Non-geographical numbers (convergent services: IP telephony, etc.).

These numbers take the form SABPQMCDU, in which S = 9.

–            The list of numbers SABPQMCDU currently attributed to the operator Orange (Sonatel S.A) for its fixed telephony networks is as follows:

V.  National calls

In order to call a subscriber to the national fixed or mobile telecommunication networks (local or national call), a number of format SABPQMCDU is used.

VI. Calls to emergency services

The numbers used to contact one of the emergency services (two or three digits) from within the country take the following format:

1X - where        X = 8 fire service and X = 7 police

These services cannot be called from outside the country.

Important notes:

(1)         All collect calls destined to public call boxes should be blocked by the operator of the originating country.

(2)         All calls to the destination 44 XX XX should be blocked by the carrier from the originating country. These sequences are reserved for special numbers in French Polynesia (audiotext …).

(3)         All collect calls to GSM/UMTS mobile numbers should be blocked by the operator of the originating country. All other type of calls has to be authorized by the originating country carrier to all GSM/UMTS mobile number ranges.

              Any collect calls received on these numbering sequences in French Polynesia will not be included in the international settlements.

Morocco +212

Communication of 13.V.2014

The Agence Nationale de Réglementation des Télécommunications (ANRT ), Rabat, announces the update of the national telephone numbering plan of Morocco, a closed ten-digit plan with the following format:

              CC N(S)N

where:

              CC (country code) = +212               N(S)N (national (significant) number) consisting of nine digits = ZABPQMCDU

I)           International incoming calls

International dialling format:        CC (212) + N(S)N (nine digits)

where:

 

CC

=

country code

N(S)N

=

national (significant) number

 

In the Kingdom of Morocco it is customary to consider, in the format +212 ZABPQMCDU the successive digits following a national (significant) number (N(S)N) as being represented by the following letters:

 

A

=

area code

ZBPQ

=

destination code for the home exchange

MCDU

=

thousands, hundreds, tens and units: the identity of a subscriber in a given exchange

*X:     digit from 0 to 9

 

 

II)          National calls

To place a local or national call to a fixed national public telecommunication network subscriber or to a mobile network subscriber, only one format needs to be used: 0ZABPQMCDU.

III)         Calls to special services

To obtain a two- or three-digit special service nationally, the dialling format is as follows:

              1X   –  where:     X =   5 for the fire service and X = 9 for the police               1XY –  where     XY = 77 for emergency calls to the gendarmerie royale .

These special services cannot be called from outside the country.

IV)         International outgoing calls

To place an international call from Morocco, dial the international prefix for Morocco, namely "00", i.e. the following format:

              00 CC NDC SN, where:

 

CC

=

country code

NDC

=

national destination code

SN

=

Subscriber number

 

V)          Fixed non-geographic numbers

These numbers take the form 0ZABPQMCDU, where A = 8.

Routing Prefixes for Number Portability

 

 

Table 9-1 - Description of introduction of new resource for national numbering plan for country code +355:

 

a)          Overview:

              The minimum number length (excluding the country code) is 3 digits

              The maximum number length (excluding the country code) is 9 digits

b)          Link to the national database (or any applicable list) with assigned ITU-T E.164 numbers within the national numbering plan: http://www.akep.al/images/stories/AKEP/planinumracionit/ Num_Alokuar_28140331_29-040414.zip

c)           Link to the real-time database reflecting ITU-T E.164 ported numbers: http://www.portabiliteti.al/

d)          Detail of the changes for numbering plan:

The Geografic Area Numbers in  National Numbering Plane(NNP) in Republic of Albania, passed from 36 Geografic District Area Numbers to 12 Geografic Region Area Numbers, remaining the same numbers of NDC (from January 1, 2014).

Brazil +55

Communication of 28.II.2014

The Agência Nacional de Telecomunicações (ANATEL), Brasilia, announces that the Numbering Plan of mobile services in Brazil will be modified due to the increasing demand for new numbers.

The current format of mobile numbers is N 8 N 7 N 6 N 5 N 4 N 3 N 2 N 1 and the first digit which identifies this service is 9, 8, 7 or 6. However, in accordance with Resolution No. 553, issued by the Agencia Nacional de Telecomunicaçôes (ANATEL) on 14 December 2010, there will be the inclusion of a ninth digit in mobile number length and all subscriber numbers will initiate with the digit “9”.

Therefore, mobile numbers will have the following format: +55 XX 9 XXXX XXXX (country code + area code + subscriber number).

This change was already implemented in the Area Codes 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18 and 19 (State of São Paulo ) and in the Area Codes 21, 22, 24, 27 and 28 ( States of Rio de Janeiro and Espírito Santo).

Now, in this year of 2014, the changing will occur in the Area Codes 91, 92, 93, 94, 95, 96, 97, 98, and 99 , on November 2 nd , (States of Amapá, Amazonas, Maranhão, Pará and Roraima).

ANATEL will define in the future the date in which this change will take place in the other Area Codes of Brazil.

In addition, ANATEL would like to highlight that this format change will not be applied to mobile radio service numbers nor to fixed switched telephone numbers. Consequently, subscriber numbers for these services will remain eight- digit long.

Sipme +883 (5130)

Communication of 14.I.2014

SIPME Limited , Kiryat Motzkin, recalls that the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) assigned the E.164 shared country code and identification code +883 5130 to Sipme Ltd on 16 September 2013 and it is being introduced on 1ST January 2014. Provisions must therefore be made in all countries with immediate effect, for callers to be able to dial the country code +883 5130 followed by the Subscriber Number (SN).

The initial +883 5130 dialling plan will consist of +883 5130 followed by eight (8) digits, (i.e +883 5130 XXXX XXXX).

Sipme has a Transit-Carrier Agreement with Bezeq International (Israel). Traffic to the E.164 shared country code and identification code +883 5130 received from any of your customers needs to be sent to Bezeq International for termination (Point Code 4-004-0 & 4-004-1).

Iridium Communications Inc. +8816 & 8817

Communication of 14.XI.2013

Iridium Communications Inc. Tempe, recalls that the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) has assigned country codes +881 6 and +881 7 to Iridium Communications Inc. for use in the Global Mobile Satellite Service (GMSS), also known as GMPCS, (reference Recommendation ITU-T E.164). Iridium Communications Inc. officially re-launched its commercial voice and data services on 30 March 2001. All administrations and recognized operating agencies (ROAs) are requested to include both +881 6 and +881 7 into existing country code translations as a valid code.

Iridium Communications Inc. has interconnection agreements with the following carriers listed below. At the present time, these are the only valid directly interconnected IXC carriers for terminating or originating traffic with the Iridium Network. Their local representative should be contacted for pricing and routing information:

AT&T (U.S.):       www.att.com/worldwide/ Sprint (U.S.):       www.sprint.com/ Telstra International (AUS):      www.telstrainternational.asia/ (previously known as Reach)

Iridium Communications Inc. requests that access be ensured to the Iridium network using country codes +881 6 and +881 7, and has set up a recorded announcement in its switch that will enable customers to validate their routing.

To access this service, please dial:    +881 6 311 10006 and                                                                         +881 7 311 10007

Calls placed to these numbers will terminate at Iridium Communications Inc. switch with the following recorded announcement: “You have reached the Iridium Communications Tempe Gateway, your access to the Iridium global network. Welcome.”

The contact person below would appreciate an e-mail message or fax from you with the contact information for both the person responsible for your main translations and the main technical point of contact for your company. This will allow Iridium Communications Inc. to work together with customers to solve any routing problems and other issues that might arise.
